issue: When assessing prejudice under Olano's third prong on plain-error review, may the reviewing court consider the full record, or is its review confined to the trial record?

sides.position: Reviewing court may consider the entire record (including materials beyond the trial record) when assessing whether a plain error affected substantial rights
cases: United States v. Ward, 957 F.3d 691 (6th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Reed, 941 F.3d 1018 (11th Cir. 2019)
United States v. Hollingshed, 940 F.3d 410 (8th Cir. 2019)
United States v. Benamor, 937 F.3d 1182 (9th Cir. 2019)
United States v. Medley, 972 F.3d 399 (4th Cir. 2020)

sides.position: Review for plain-error prejudice is confined to the trial record
cases: United States v. Maez, 960 F.3d 949 (7th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Miller, 954 F.3d 551 (2d Cir. 2020)

this_court: does not decide (the opinion says the Fourth Circuit has yet to determine the question, and finds no reversible plain error even on the full record)
quote: Our sister circuits are split on this issue.
cite: United States v. Jovon Medley, 972 F.3d 399 (4th Cir. 2020)
